results.Professional_Suggestions:
【B1 Camera Position】Take approximately two steps to the right and half a step forward to center the motorcycle within the frame, completely excluding the tripod leg visible on the far left edge.
【C1 Shot Size】Zoom in slightly or physically move closer until the motorcycle and rider occupy about 80% of the frame's height, reducing the empty black space on the right side.
【E1 Lighting Utilization】Tap on the motorcycle's headlight on your screen to lock focus and exposure, then drag the exposure slider down by about -1.0 to -1.5 EV to retain the intricate details of the headlamp. If using a flash, diffuse it with a softbox or bounce it off a nearby surface to create softer, more even illumination on the rider and bike.
results.Image_Editing_Prompt: Preserve the identity of the rider, the specific motorcycle model, and the rider's gear exactly as they are. The ideal final image is a striking night portrait of a motorcyclist. The subject is perfectly centered in the frame (Subject Placement), sitting confidently on the bike with a poised posture (Pose & Expression). The camera is positioned at a low, eye-level angle relative to the rider's chest, creating an imposing and heroic perspective (Camera Position & Angle). The framing is a tight medium shot, with the motorcycle and rider occupying the majority of the frame, eliminating unnecessary empty space and peripheral distractions (Shot Size). The depth of field is moderate, keeping both the rider and the motorcycle in sharp focus while the background gently falls off into darkness (Depth of Field). The lighting is dramatic but controlled; the headlight is properly exposed, revealing the intricate mechanical details of the lamp without blowing out, while the rider is illuminated by soft, diffused light that highlights the textures of the leather and gear (Lighting Utilization). The overall color palette features a moody, high-contrast aesthetic with deep blacks, accented by the vibrant orange of the bike's wheels and the cool, cinematic tones of the rider's gear (Color & Tonal Key). The background is a clean, deep black void, ensuring the viewer's attention remains entirely on the illuminated subject (Background).
